# Code of conduct

## Where this applies

Issues, pull requests, commit messages, and anywhere somebody is speaking for
this project. It applies to everyone equally, the maintainer included — a code
of conduct that exempts whoever wrote it is a statement about power rather than
about behavior.

## What this project is for

It is a worked example of a method, so the contribution worth most here is an
argument about a decision: a record that does not hold up, a rule that costs
more than it buys, a claim that is false.
[docs/adr/](../docs/adr/README.md) is where that reasoning lives, and
disagreeing with it is close to the point of publishing any of it.

The distinction this page rests on: *this decision is wrong, and here is what it
produces* is the work. *You are careless* is not a sharper version of the same
thing — it is a different thing, and it ends the conversation the first one was
starting.

## What is expected

- **Argue about the claim.** A record, a rule, a wrong sentence, a missing case.
- **Say what you actually observed**, and keep it apart from what you concluded.
- **Assume the other person read carefully and disagrees anyway.** Most of the
  time that is what happened.
- **Let a decision be a decision.** A maintainer who says no and gives a reason
  has answered you. How an accepted record is changed is written down, and
  reopening the same argument in a new issue is not that route.

## What is not acceptable

- Harassment, sustained hostility, or aggression aimed at a person rather than
  at a claim.
- Insults or dismissal based on who somebody is — nationality, ethnicity, sex,
  gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, religion, appearance or
  first language. **English is the language of this repository and the second or
  third language of many people reading it.** Treating imperfect English as
  evidence about the argument belongs squarely in this list.
- Publishing anybody's private information, or something shared with you
  privately.
- Sexual attention or imagery.
- Deliberately wasting people's time: arguments made to provoke, or bad-faith
  reports under this document.

## Reporting

Email **nanatsusaya@mein.gmx**. What happened, where, and roughly when. A link
is enough; nobody owes a summary of something unpleasant.

**Reporting the maintainer is a legitimate use of that address**, and so is
asking whether something is worth reporting before deciding.

## What happens then

One person reads that mailbox, so there is no committee and this document does
not pretend there is one. There is **no promised response time.** A report that
gets no answer at all is more likely to have gone missing than to have been
ignored — send it again rather than assuming.

The report stays private. A name is not passed on without agreement, including
to the person reported, and where a response would identify you regardless you
are told that before anything happens. Not every report ends in action; one
that does not still gets an answer saying so and why.

## What this document does not do

It does not settle a technical disagreement and it is not a route to winning
one. And it reaches only the places named at the top.
